title: Bishop Vs Queen: Win the Promotion Race
summary: After the king accepts the bishop sacrifice, push immediately: the new queen controls the opponent’s promotion square.

nodes.question: The bishop is gone. What matters more than capturing another pawn?
nodes.explanation: White’s h6 pawn needs two moves to promote. Black’s a3 pawn also needs two moves, but White moves first and Qh8 will control a1. Every king move gives up the win; h7 is the only winning move in this exact position.

branches.title: Source reply to the bishop capture: promote first
commentary: Begin after ...Kxe4 at 96 seconds. The bishop has been removed, leaving seven pieces. The earlier eight-piece bishop offer and the other source branches remain outside this proof.
h7 uses the first tempo to approach promotion. White’s king stays on d7; capturing a central pawn instead would lose the race with best defense.
a2 advances Black’s fastest passer. It threatens promotion next move, but White is already ready to queen.
h8=Q promotes first. The diagonal h8–g7–f6–e5–d4–c3–b2–a1 is clear, so the queen controls Black’s promotion square. This complete queen-versus-four-pawns position is an exact White win.

branches.title: Independent continuation: answer a queen promotion
commentary: The first three moves follow the source’s pawn race. The subsequent black promotion and queen capture are an independently added illustration of the open diagonal.
h7 preserves White’s forced win by using the next tempo for promotion.
a2 threatens to queen but leaves the long diagonal unobstructed.
h8=Q creates the queen before Black can promote. It already attacks a1 from the opposite corner.
a1=Q is legal and creates a queen, but it arrives on a square attacked by Qh8. This is a representative losing defense, not a move claimed to be shown in the video.
Qxa1 captures the new queen along the open diagonal. White wins the resulting queen-versus-three-pawns ending; the lesson stops before inventing a complete conversion.

branches.title: Independent mistake: collect a pawn instead
commentary: Compare a tempting pawn capture before pushing. This is independent analysis of the visually reconstructed seven-piece position.
Kxe6 takes a central pawn but gives Black the first advance in the promotion race. The exact outcome changes to a Black win; material gain has cost the essential tempo.
a2 brings Black’s pawn one step from queening while White’s h-pawn is still on h6. White can no longer achieve the source’s promote-first diagonal control with best defense.

exercises.prompt: Why does the new queen stop a faraway pawn?
exercises.answer: Qh8 controls a1 along an unobstructed diagonal. If Black promotes to a queen there, Qxa1 captures it.

exercises.prompt: Why not take e6 before pushing?
exercises.answer: The pawn capture spends the move White needs to reach h8 first. The exact comparison loses with best play, whereas h7 preserves the win.
